sentences.text:
Order 
T his is the first application filed by applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.82 of 2024 registered at Police Station Mohgaon, District-Mandla for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376 (2) (N) and 306 of IPC.
As per the prosecution case, the allegations against the present applicant is that he and deceased used to live as husband and wife in Aurangabad for about 2 months.
Thereafter, they returned to their village.
Accused refused to marry the deceased thats why she committed suicide.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 03.04.2024.
Applicant and deceased were having love affair and they used to live with each other for about 2 months in Aurangabad as husband and wife.
Applicant has never refused to marry the deceased Deceased was aged about 22 years and she was having two months pregnancy at the time of incident.
There is nothing on record to show that the applicant has abetted the deceased 2 MCRC-21199-2024 to commit suicide.
Therefore, no offence under Section 306 of IPC is made out against the applicant.
He has been falsely implicated in the case.
Earlier hearing of this case is not possible in near future.
On above grounds, it has been prayed that applicant be released on bail.
Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State on the other hand has opposed the bail application.

I have heard both learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

Keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case and including the nature of evidence available on record, I deem it appropriate to allow this application.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
